fields.label: Scheme Name
fields.description: What the offer is called in conversation. Nothing about the outcome depends on the wording - two schemes that both claim the same items are ordered by priority and then by this record id, never by name, because a name is typed by a person and may hold characters a phone and a server sort differently.

fields.label: Type
fields.options:
Volume Slab
Value Slab
Combo
Flat Offer
Free Goods
Rep Incentive
fields.description: How a manager files the offer for reporting. The engine reads the basis, the measure and the slabs and never looks at this, so changing it re-labels a scheme without re-pricing a single order.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: Lower runs first. Where two schemes claim the same items this is how a manager says which one wins, and it is the only place that intent can be expressed - the engine breaks a remaining tie on the record id so that two phones and the server never reach different answers.

fields.label: Active
fields.description: Switches a running scheme off without cancelling it. Cancelling would take the accruals already sitting in the ledger with it, and those are what a distributor claims against at month end.

fields.label: Funded By
fields.description: Who bears the cost of what this scheme gives away. A benefit the distributor funds becomes a claim at month end and one we fund does not, and a ledger row cannot be reconciled by anyone who does not know which of the two it is.

fields.label: Basis
fields.description: Whether a slab is crossed by how much was bought or by what it was worth.

fields.label: Slab Units
fields.description: The unit the slab numbers below are typed in. Schemes are written on a whiteboard in cases because that is how a shopkeeper orders; the compiler converts to base units once, on the server, so the engine is handed whole numbers and never divides by a conversion factor it would have to look up.

fields.label: Measured Over
fields.description: Whether the measure totals only the qualifying items or the whole cart. An Item Set scheme with an empty item table qualifies on nothing at all and would quietly never fire, so it is refused at save.

fields.label: Stacking
fields.description: Exclusive claims every item it qualified on and drops any later scheme that overlaps them. Stackable runs alongside anything. Best Of Group keeps only the single richest scheme inside one group, which is how two competing offers on the same brand are presented to a shopkeeper as one number instead of two.

fields.label: Stack Group
fields.description: The label the competing schemes share. Best Of Group with no group is a scheme competing against nothing, which reads as a limit and behaves as none.

fields.label: Valid To
fields.description: Blank leaves the scheme open-ended. Dates are compared on the server when the spec is compiled and never on the device, because a phone clock is something a rep can change and an expired offer is not something a rep should be able to reopen.

fields.label: Booked From
fields.description: An EARLY-BOOKING window, and a different question from Valid From above. Valid From is when this offer is live; this is when the order has to have been TAKEN to earn it. A season scheme is typically live from November to March - because that is when it is billed - and rewards only the orders booked in November. Blank means any order date, which is every ordinary scheme.

fields.label: Requires Advance
fields.description: Only bookings of a season that asks for at least this much up front earn this offer. Read against the SEASON's advance, not against what has been paid so far: the order is priced the moment it is taken and no advance has arrived yet, and a booking cannot be released without its season's advance anyway - so the two come to the same thing by the time anything is billed. Blank or zero asks for nothing, which is every ordinary scheme.

fields.label: Budget
fields.description: The total this scheme may give away, in rupees. Blank means uncapped, which is a decision somebody should have made rather than one that happened.

fields.label: Consumed
fields.description: What the scheme ledger has already accrued against this scheme, discounts and the cost of free goods together. Held here rather than summed on demand so a phone can be told what is left without running a query it has no connection to run.

fields.label: When The Budget Runs Out
fields.description: Block drops the scheme whole once the budget is gone - never part of it, because a half-funded offer is a number nobody can reconcile afterwards. Warn keeps granting and flags every order that lands after the pot is empty, which is the right answer when stopping a promise already being made at a counter costs more than the overspend.

fields.label: Applies To
fields.description: Which kind of sale this scheme is for. Secondary is an order at a shop, which the distributor bills. Primary is an order on a party we bill ourselves. A scheme written for one must not fire on the other - a retailer offer landing on a distributor's own purchase is trade spend nobody budgeted.

fields.label: Scope
fields.description: No rows at all means everywhere. Territory is matched down the tree rather than by name, so a row sitting at the root - which is what Frappe writes into an empty Territory link from the session defaults of whoever opened the form - still means everywhere instead of meaning nothing. That exact injection once made checklist templates disappear with no error anywhere.

fields.label: Applies Everywhere
fields.description: Set at save when nothing in the scope table actually narrows the scheme. A manager who meant to pilot an offer in one district and sees this ticked has found the mistake before the budget does.

fields.label: Items
fields.description: What has to be bought for the scheme to count. Groups and brands are expanded to plain item codes by the compiler, so the list a phone evaluates against holds no tree and no lookup.

fields.label: Slabs
fields.description: One row per benefit, rows sharing a slab number making one slab that grants a combo. Slabs must ascend and must not overlap: the engine taking the highest matching slab is a safety net, not a policy, and a cart that could land in two slabs at once is a scheme nobody can explain to the shopkeeper it was quoted to.

fields.label: Reads As
fields.description: The whole offer in one sentence a rep can say out loud. Anything a rep has to read off a slab table at a counter does not get said at all.

fields.label: Spec Version
fields.description: Raised whenever the rules themselves change - slabs, items, scope, basis, validity or budget - and left alone when only the wording moves. A phone prices against a compiled spec it cached at the last pull, so this is the number that says which version of the offer a rep is quoting at a counter today.

fields.label: Compiled On
fields.description: When the current rules were last compiled and handed to sync. Edited after this timestamp and every rep in the field is still quoting the previous version until their next pull, which is correct and has to be visible rather than silent.
